text.p: These are the leading stories in the Lebanese press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Former Hizbollah leader Sheikh Sobhi Tufaili welcomes troops sent to muzzle protesters.
Tufaili is leading a "hunger revolt" in the form of a civil disobedience campaign to highlight poverty in Lebanon.
- Five Japanese Red Army members sentenced to prison by a Lebanese court last month appeal for a retrial.
- The South Lebanon Army withdraws troops from a key position in the Jezzine region of Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone.
- Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri says sectarian feelings are the source of Lebanon's problems.
- Surprising South Lebanon Army withdrawal from position in south Lebanon.
- Army units deployed in Baalbek in the Bekaa Valley.
The Lebanese government has decided to deploy extra army troops in parts of the Bekaa Valley and the southern suburbs of Beirut to quell a civil disobedience campaign.
- President Elias Hrawi says the regional situation is difficult but there is no danger of war.
